lessons.title: Escape the Commodity Trap
lessons.key_idea: When your offer looks like everyone else's, buyers compare on price, so you need a unique Grand Slam Offer that cannot be compared.

lessons.title: Find a Starving Crowd
lessons.key_idea: The market you choose matters more than your offer or your persuasion skills, so pick people with urgent pain, money to spend, easy access, and a growing need.

lessons.title: Charge More, Not Less
lessons.key_idea: Premium prices create a virtuous cycle, because more margin lets you deliver better results and attract more committed customers.

lessons.title: The Value Equation
lessons.key_idea: Value rises with the dream outcome and the buyer's belief they will get it, and it falls with the time it takes and the effort it costs.

lessons.title: Turn Problems Into a Stacked Offer
lessons.key_idea: List every obstacle your customer faces, turn each into a solution, choose how to deliver it, then trim and stack the best pieces into one package.

lessons.title: Enhance With Scarcity, Bonuses, Guarantees
lessons.key_idea: Scarcity, urgency, bonuses, guarantees and a compelling name make a strong offer even harder to refuse.

lessons.title: Making People Feel Stupid Saying No
lessons.key_idea: The right crowd, a confident price, the value equation and smart enhancers combine into an offer that sells itself.

plan.title: $100M Offers
plan.author: Alex Hormozi
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's core frameworks well, including the Grand Slam Offer, the starving crowd, the value equation, and the offer enhancers, though I would leave out fine details I am unsure of.
plan.one_liner: Stop competing on price. Build an offer so valuable that saying no feels foolish.
plan.summary: Alex Hormozi argues that most businesses struggle not because of weak marketing, but because their offer is ordinary. When you sell the same thing as everyone else, buyers compare on price, and everyone races to the bottom. His answer is the Grand Slam Offer, a package so valuable that turning it down feels foolish. First, he shows how to choose a starving crowd: people with urgent pain, money to spend, and easy access. He explains why charging more can make you better at serving customers. At the heart of the book is a value equation. You raise the dream outcome and the buyer's belief it will happen, while cutting the waiting time and the effort required. Then you list every obstacle your customer faces, turn each one into a solution, and bundle them together. Scarcity, urgency, bonuses, guarantees and smart naming make the offer even stronger.
